Thank you for sharing this — wanting to change is a really meaningful first step. Negative thinking can become such a habit that it feels like the default, but it is something that can shift with practice over time.

One helpful approach is to start noticing negative thoughts without judging yourself for having them. When you catch one, gently ask, "Is there another way to look at this?" You don't have to force positivity — even neutrality can be progress. Small practices like writing down one thing each day that went okay, even something simple, can slowly retrain your brain to notice different things. Also, consider whether talking with a counselor or therapist might help — they can offer personalized tools, especially if this pattern feels deeply rooted or connected to other struggles.

Be patient with yourself. Changing thought patterns takes time, and setbacks don't mean you're failing. The fact that you want to grow in this way says a lot about your self-awareness and resilience.
